feedback.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.35$ | $0.15$ |

Compute ${f}_{X|Y}(4\,|\,2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
The conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=y).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(4\,|\,2)=P(X=4\,|\,Y=2).
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X=4\,|\,Y=2)=\frac{P(X=4,Y=2)}{P(Y=2)}=\frac{f(4,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(2) & =f(2,2)+f(4,2) \\  & =0.4+0.15 \\  & =0.55.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, $f(4,2)=0.15.$ 

Finally, substituting  ${f}_{Y}(2)=0.55$ and $f(4,2)=0.15$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(4\,|\,2) & =P(X=4\,|\,Y=2) \\  & =\frac{f(4,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)} \\  & =\frac{0.15}{0.55} \\  & ≈0.27.\end{aligned}
$$
